name: Event And Gap Reversion
rationale: Gap and event-style rules test whether large overnight or single-day moves mean-revert after delayed execution.
expected_benefit: Potential short-horizon opportunity after sharp moves, with explicit attention to execution realism.
failure_modes: Gap moves can continue instead of reverting.
Daily bars may hide intraday risk.
Entry timing can make the signal untradeable after next-open delay.

canonical_variants.name: Large down-gap reversion
canonical_variants.description: Enter after a large overnight down gap and exit after a fixed recovery condition.
canonical_variants.hypothesis_template: A large down-gap reversion rule may capture panic overreaction after delayed next-open execution.
canonical_variants.minimum_acceptable_performance: Improve Sharpe after costs and show acceptable worst trade behavior.

canonical_variants.name: Large up-gap fade
canonical_variants.description: Avoid or fade exposure after unusually large up gaps.
canonical_variants.hypothesis_template: A large up-gap fade may avoid buying short-term exhaustion after unusually strong overnight moves.
canonical_variants.minimum_acceptable_performance: Improve Sharpe while retaining at least 60% of benchmark CAGR.

canonical_variants.name: Large down-day recovery
canonical_variants.description: Enter after a large close-to-close down day and exit after recovery.
canonical_variants.hypothesis_template: A large down-day recovery rule may capture short-term reversal after broad selloffs.
canonical_variants.minimum_acceptable_performance: Improve Sharpe and keep max drawdown no worse than buy-and-hold.

suggested_validation: Track trade count and worst trade.
Do not trust results if signals are too sparse.
references: Short-term reversal and gap-trading practitioner literature
Execution realism notes for daily-bar systems
execution_notes: The current strategy schema lacks prior-close arithmetic, gap calculations, and fixed holding-period exits.
